answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a delta as the anchor of the cost.
